ops.name: Owner
ops.description: Business owner who reviews the financial picture and makes decisions.

ops.name: Bookkeeper
ops.description: Person who maintains the numbers and uploads the Excel files.

ops.name: Manager
ops.description: Department lead who views figures for their own area.

ops.name: Accountant
ops.description: External advisor who reviews period totals for tax and reporting.

ops.name: Excel Upload
ops.description: A source spreadsheet imported to feed the dashboard.
ops.example: Financials_2024_Q1.xlsx uploaded by Bookkeeper on Apr 2

ops.name: Account Line
ops.description: A single row from the spreadsheet tying a category to an amount.

ops.name: Category
ops.description: A grouping of income or expense lines.

ops.name: Period
ops.description: A month, quarter, or year the figures belong to.

ops.name: Revenue Figure
ops.description: Total income recorded for a period.

ops.name: Expense Figure
ops.description: Total spending recorded for a period.

ops.name: Profit Summary
ops.description: Revenue minus expenses for a period.

ops.name: Dashboard View
ops.description: A saved arrangement of charts and totals someone looks at.

ops.name: User
ops.description: A person with access to the dashboard.

ops.example: Bookkeeper maps 'Rent' column to Office Rent category
Bookkeeper fixes a mistyped $3,200 rent amount
Owner views Q1 2024 net profit of $38,000
Bookkeeper reopens Q1 to fix a figure
Owner saves a new Cash Flow view
Owner invites Jane as a Manager

ops.text: Only the Owner and Bookkeeper may upload or edit spreadsheets and figures; Managers and Accountants can only view.
ops.example: Manager Jane cannot upload a new Excel file

ops.text: A Manager may only see figures for the areas assigned to them, not the whole company.
ops.example: Marketing Manager sees Marketing expenses but not Payroll

ops.text: A period must be uploaded and mapped before its figures appear on any dashboard.
ops.example: Q2 2024 shows no totals until its file is uploaded

ops.text: Once a period is closed, its figures cannot be edited unless it is reopened by the Owner.
ops.example: Closed Q1 figures are locked from edits

ops.text: Profit Summary must always equal Revenue Figure minus Expense Figure for the same period.
Every Account Line must belong to exactly one Category and one Period.
ops.example: A rent line cannot be left uncategorized

ops.text: All amounts are recorded in a single currency across all uploads.
ops.example: A euro-denominated line is rejected or converted before import

ops.text: Re-uploading a file for a period replaces the prior figures rather than adding to them.
ops.example: Uploading Q1 twice does not double revenue

ops.text: Does not connect to bank accounts or pull transactions automatically.
Does not generate or send invoices to customers.
Does not file taxes or produce official accounting statements.
Does not let external clients or the public log in.
Does not handle payroll processing or payments.

ops.question: Who needs an account to use the app?

options.label: Nobody logs in — one person uses it on their own device
Exactly one person logs in (the owner)
Several people log in, possibly with different powers

ops.question: Do different people have different powers?

options.label: Everyone who logs in can do everything
An owner/admin plus staff with fewer powers
Admins define their own roles and permissions

ops.question: Is this for one business, or will many separate businesses use it with their data kept apart?

options.label: Many separate businesses, each seeing only its own data

ops.question: How do additional people get access?
How do people sign in?
What happens when two people edit the same thing at once?

options.label: Common; the app must prevent or merge conflicting edits

ops.question: Do you need a record of who changed what and when?

options.label: Just created/updated by whom and when
A full, viewable history of every change

ops.question: How does the app reach people when something happens?

options.label: It doesn't — people check the app

ops.question: Must it work without internet?

options.label: Keeps working offline and syncs later

ops.question: Where is it used?

options.label: In a browser, on desktop and phone
In a browser, mostly on phones

ops.question: Do you start with existing data?
Do people need to get their data out?
When something is deleted, what really happens?

options.label: It's archived and can be restored
Records are never deleted, only voided/cancelled

ops.question: How much data will there be?
Languages and regions?
Can files/photos be attached to things?

options.label: Yes — with previews, versions, and sharing

ops.question: Do some actions need someone else's approval first?
Does it hold data with special legal handling (health, payment cards, minors)?
How long is data kept?

options.label: Each business sets its own policy

ops.question: Can each business customize the app?

options.label: No — everyone gets the same thing

ops.question: What do people need to see across many records?

options.label: A dashboard with totals and counts

ops.question: Are records grouped into separate projects/workspaces, or is it one shared pool?

options.label: One shared pool — everything lives in one place with filters
Separate projects/workspaces, each with its own members

ops.question: Who can see a record?

options.label: Everyone in the team sees everything
Records are private to their owner unless shared or assigned
Visible within the owner's team/department; admins see all

ops.question: Who can change a record?

options.label: Anyone who can see it can edit it
Only its owner/assignee and admins; others just view
Set per record: view / comment / edit

ops.question: Are the fields on a record fixed, or can admins add their own?

options.label: Fixed — the same fields for everyone
Admins add custom fields (text, number, date, dropdown) to each record type
Admins define whole new record types with their own fields

ops.question: Should the app do things on its own when records change?

options.label: No — people do everything by hand
Simple rules: when X happens, notify/assign/change stage
Multi-step workflows with conditions and delays

ops.question: Can two records be the same thing (same email, same serial number)?

options.label: The app warns about likely duplicates and offers to merge
A key field must be unique; duplicates are rejected

ops.question: How do people find a record?

options.label: Filter and sort within each list
One search box across all record types
Search that also looks inside comments and attachments

ops.question: When a file is re-uploaded for a period (r8 replace), how are prior figures and manual corrections handled?

options.label: Wipe and replace all lines for the period
Keep prior version, switch active, allow rollback

ops.question: Can a closed period be reopened, and what happens to figures and audit when it is?
If an Excel upload parses partway then hits a bad row, what happens?

options.label: Import valid rows, flag bad ones for fixing

ops.question: How are spreadsheet rows with no matching Category treated (r6 requires exactly one)?

options.label: Block period from showing until all rows mapped

ops.question: How is a Manager restricted to their assigned areas, and can totals leak?

options.label: Only assigned categories; company totals hidden
Assigned detail plus company-wide aggregate figures
Owner can delegate extra areas per manager

ops.question: How are negative amounts, refunds, and rounding handled in figures?
How are periods and overlapping/misaligned dates resolved?
How is the single-currency rule enforced on import?

options.label: Assume all files are in the org's configured currency
Detect other currencies and reject the file
Detect and convert at a set rate

stated in the description: a12: Owner invites users.
stated in the description: Core flow is importing Excel files (a1).
stated in the description: r2: managers see only their area; owner sees all.
stated in the description: r1: only Owner/Bookkeeper edit; others view.
stated in the description: App is a dashboard of totals (Profit Summary, figures) with saved views.
stated in the description: r7: single currency across all uploads; one business.

sheet.one_liner: internal dashboard based on our excel files with financials

actors.name: Owner
actors.description: Business owner who reviews the financial picture and makes decisions.

actors.name: Bookkeeper
actors.description: Person who maintains the numbers and uploads the Excel files.

actors.name: Manager
actors.description: Department lead who views figures for their own area.

actors.name: Accountant
actors.description: External advisor who reviews period totals for tax and reporting.

nouns.name: Excel Upload
nouns.description: A source spreadsheet imported to feed the dashboard.
nouns.example: Financials_2024_Q1.xlsx uploaded by Bookkeeper on Apr 2

nouns.name: Account Line
nouns.description: A single row from the spreadsheet tying a category to an amount.

nouns.name: Category
nouns.description: A grouping of income or expense lines.

nouns.name: Period
nouns.description: A month, quarter, or year the figures belong to.

nouns.name: Revenue Figure
nouns.description: Total income recorded for a period.

nouns.name: Expense Figure
nouns.description: Total spending recorded for a period.

nouns.name: Profit Summary
nouns.description: Revenue minus expenses for a period.

nouns.name: Dashboard View
nouns.description: A saved arrangement of charts and totals someone looks at.

nouns.name: User
nouns.description: A person with access to the dashboard.

actions.example: Bookkeeper uploads Financials_2024_Q1.xlsx
Bookkeeper maps 'Rent' column to Office Rent category
Bookkeeper fixes a mistyped $3,200 rent amount
Owner views Q1 2024 net profit of $38,000
Owner opens Monthly Overview
Manager views Marketing spend of $9,400
Owner closes Q1 2024 after review
Accountant reviews Q1 2024 revenue of $148,000
Bookkeeper reopens Q1 to fix a figure
Owner saves a new Cash Flow view
Bookkeeper adds a 'Software' expense category
Owner invites Jane as a Manager

rules.text: Only the Owner and Bookkeeper may upload or edit spreadsheets and figures; Managers and Accountants can only view.
rules.example: Manager Jane cannot upload a new Excel file

rules.text: A Manager may only see figures for the areas assigned to them, not the whole company.
rules.example: Marketing Manager sees Marketing expenses but not Payroll

rules.text: A period must be uploaded and mapped before its figures appear on any dashboard.
rules.example: Q2 2024 shows no totals until its file is uploaded

rules.text: Once a period is closed, its figures cannot be edited unless it is reopened by the Owner.
rules.example: Closed Q1 figures are locked from edits

rules.text: Profit Summary must always equal Revenue Figure minus Expense Figure for the same period.
Every Account Line must belong to exactly one Category and one Period.
rules.example: A rent line cannot be left uncategorized

rules.text: All amounts are recorded in a single currency across all uploads.
rules.example: A euro-denominated line is rejected or converted before import

rules.text: Re-uploading a file for a period replaces the prior figures rather than adding to them.
rules.example: Uploading Q1 twice does not double revenue

rules.text: Only the Owner may invite users, assign roles, and change what areas a user can access; Bookkeepers, Managers, and Accountants cannot manage user accounts.
Every upload, correction, and period close/reopen must be recorded with who did it and when, and this history cannot be altered.
Each User must have a role and (for Managers) their allowed areas assigned when they are invited.
A Category cannot be deleted while Account Lines are still assigned to it; the lines must be reassigned or removed first.
An Excel Upload must have a file, a period covered, and an uploader recorded before it can be imported.
Each Period label must be unique, so figures are never split across two records for the same month, quarter, or year.

non_goals.text: Does not connect to bank accounts or pull transactions automatically.
Does not generate or send invoices to customers.
Does not file taxes or produce official accounting statements.
Does not let external clients or the public log in.
Does not handle payroll processing or payments.
